einzeiler: Malcolm Gladwell discusses podcasting, political satire, and his series Revisionist…
kurzfassung: Malcolm Gladwell reflects on the transition from writing to podcasting in front of a live audience. He explores the limits and paradoxes of political satire using examples from the US, UK, and Israel. He also addresses audience questions about higher education funding, historical assumptions, and human emotions.
stichpunkte: Malcolm Gladwell discusses the psychological and emotional nuances of hosting an audio podcast.
He examines the 'Loads of Money' character in British comedy to explore the limits of political satire.
Communication scholar Heather Lamar's research on The Colbert Report reveals how audiences view satire through biased perception.
Jonathan Coe's writing highlights how laughter can serve as a distraction from confronting serious political problems.
An Israeli television show demonstrates how satire can tackle darker, higher-stakes political realities.
Gladwell critiques the massive endowments of elite American universities and their misallocation of resources.
He explains his motivation behind Revisionist History as questioning established historical narratives shaped by victors.

kapitel.titel: The Loads of Money Problem and Satire
The Colbert Report and Motivated Cognition
Audience Q&A on Education and History

beschreibung: New York Times best-selling author Malcolm Gladwell (The Tipping Point, Outliers) talks with Virginia Heffernan about Revisionist History.
